title: Year 1-2 Thinking Skills
provenance: AWenture original practice; adapted from Alistair Thinking Skills Group 1 pack, 11 November 2026. Multiple-choice practice, not official competition questions.

questions.question: What comes next? 2, 4, 6, 8, ___
questions.explanation: 10. Add 2 each time.

questions.question: What shape comes next in the picture?
questions.explanation: Circle. The repeating unit is circle, square, triangle.

questions.question: What comes next? 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, ___
questions.explanation: 10. The steps repeat: add 1, then add 2.

questions.question: What comes next? 20, 17, 14, 11, ___
questions.explanation: 8. Subtract 3 each time.

questions.question: What letter comes next? A, C, E, G, ___
questions.explanation: I. Skip one alphabet letter each time.

questions.question: What comes next? 1, 3, 6, 10, ___
questions.explanation: 15. Add 2, then 3, then 4, then 5.

questions.question: A star means 4. What is star + star + 2?
questions.explanation: 10. Replace each star with 4: 4 + 4 + 2.

questions.question: Find the missing number: ___ + 6 = 14
questions.explanation: 8. 14 minus 6 is 8.

questions.question: Two bags hold equal numbers of marbles. They hold 12 marbles altogether. How many are in each bag?
questions.explanation: 6. Split 12 into two equal groups.

questions.question: A machine adds 3. You put in 8. What comes out?
A machine turns 2 into 5 and 4 into 9. Its rule is: double the number, then add 1. What does 6 become?
questions.explanation: 13. Double 6 is 12; add 1.

questions.question: Two stars and one moon total 13. One star is 5. What is one moon?
questions.explanation: 3. Two stars total 10, leaving 3.

questions.question: Mia is taller than Leo. Leo is taller than Sam. Who is shortest?
questions.explanation: Sam. The order from tallest is Mia, Leo, Sam.

questions.question: A red, blue and green box each hold one toy. The car is in the blue box. The bear is not in the red box. Which box holds the bear?
questions.explanation: Green. Blue holds the car; red is ruled out.

questions.question: Every zorb has a tail. Pip is a zorb. Must Pip have a tail?
questions.explanation: Yes. The rule applies to every zorb, including Pip.

questions.question: Some birds are white. Coco is a bird. Must Coco be white?
questions.explanation: No. Some does not mean all; Coco could be another colour.

questions.question: Ava, Ben and Cy each have one different pet: cat, dog or fish. Ava has the fish. Ben does not have the dog. What pet does Cy have?
questions.explanation: Dog. Ben must have the cat, so Cy has the dog.

questions.question: A red box says "The coin is in this box." A blue box says "The coin is in the red box." Exactly one box holds a coin. Could exactly one of these two statements be true?
questions.explanation: No. Both statements say the coin is in red, so both are true or both are false.

questions.question: Which shape has no straight sides? Choose its letter.
questions.explanation: C. The circle has no straight sides.

questions.question: How many small squares are shaded in the picture?
questions.explanation: 5. Count once across each row: 2 + 1 + 2.

questions.question: How many squares of ALL sizes are in the picture?
questions.explanation: 5. Four small squares and one large square.

questions.question: Finish the bottom row. Choose the missing shape.
questions.explanation: Triangle. Each row has circle, square, triangle in that order.

questions.question: A large square has one diagonal drawn from its top-left corner to its bottom-right corner. How many triangles does that make inside the square?
questions.explanation: 2. The diagonal splits the square into two triangles.

questions.question: How many triangles of ALL sizes can you see?
questions.explanation: 8. Four small triangles and four larger triangles, each made of two small ones.

questions.question: You face north. Turn right once. Which direction do you face?
questions.explanation: East. A right turn from north points east.

questions.question: You face east. Turn left once. Which direction do you face?
questions.explanation: North. A left turn from east points north.

questions.question: Start at the dot. Move 2 squares right and 1 square up. Choose the letter of your finishing square.
questions.explanation: B. The dot is in the bottom-left cell; two right and one up reaches B.

questions.question: An arrow points up. Turn it a half-turn. Which way does it point now?
questions.explanation: Down. A half-turn is 180 degrees.

questions.question: Fold a square paper exactly in half so the left edge meets the right edge. What shape is the folded paper?
questions.explanation: Rectangle. Its width is half its original width.

questions.question: Stack 3 cubes in one tower and 2 cubes in another tower beside it. The towers share no cubes. How many cubes altogether, including hidden ones?
questions.explanation: 5. Count 3 + 2; cubes still count when hidden.

questions.question: You have 3 apples. You take away 2 and hold them. How many apples are you holding?
questions.explanation: 2. The question asks about the apples you took.

questions.question: You pass the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
questions.explanation: Second. You take that runner's position.

questions.question: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. There are only 3 people: a grandfather, his son and his grandson. How can there be two fathers?
options: The grandfather and his son are both fathers.
Each person has two fathers in the boat.
questions.answer: The grandfather and his son are both fathers.
questions.explanation: The grandfather is a father, and his son is also a father.

questions.question: A toy train has no engine battery and no motor. Can it move if Alistair pushes it?
questions.explanation: Yes. A push can move it; a motor is not needed.

questions.question: A box holds 5 red socks and 5 blue socks. Without looking, what is the fewest socks you must take to be certain of two socks of the same colour?
questions.explanation: 3. The first two could be different; the third must match one of them.

questions.question: There are 4 corners on a square table. You cut off ONE corner with one straight cut, joining two adjacent sides. How many corners does the remaining tabletop have?
questions.explanation: 5. One old corner goes, but the cut creates two new corners.

questions.question: A pencil costs 3 tokens. How many tokens do 3 pencils cost?
You have 10 beads. Give 2 to Mia and 3 to Leo. How many are left?
Four children each shake hands once with every other child. How many handshakes are there?
questions.explanation: 6. Count pairs: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD.

questions.question: A snail climbs 3 steps each day, then slips down 1 step each night. It starts at step 0. On which day does it first reach step 7?
questions.explanation: Day 3. Daytime heights are 3, 5, 7. It reaches 7 before slipping.

questions.question: A toy costs 8 tokens. You can pay using only 2-token and 5-token coins. What is the fewest coins you can use to pay exactly 8?
questions.explanation: 4 coins. Four 2-token coins make 8. A 5-token coin leaves 3, which cannot be made.

questions.question: Alistair can choose a red or blue shirt and black, white or green shorts. How many different shirt-and-shorts outfits can he make?
questions.explanation: 6. Each of 2 shirts pairs with 3 shorts: 2 x 3.

questions.question: What comes next? 3, 6, 9, 12, ___
questions.explanation: 15. Add 3 each time.

questions.question: What comes next? 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, ___
questions.explanation: 11. Alternate adding 1 and adding 2.

questions.question: A triangle means 3. A square means 4. What is triangle + square + square?
Three equal baskets hold 15 balls altogether. How many balls are in each?
questions.explanation: 5. 15 split equally into 3 groups is 5.

questions.question: Jo finished before Kim. Kim finished before Lou. Who finished last?
questions.explanation: Lou. The order is Jo, Kim, Lou.

questions.question: All wugs are green. Max is green. Must Max be a wug?
questions.explanation: No. Other things may also be green.

questions.question: How many squares of ALL sizes are in this picture?
questions.explanation: 14. Nine small squares, four 2-by-2 squares and one 3-by-3 square.

questions.question: A square has 4 sides. A triangle has 3. How many sides altogether on 2 separate squares and 1 separate triangle?
You face south. Turn left once. Which direction do you face?
questions.explanation: East. Imagine facing down a map; your left is east.

questions.question: An arrow points right. Turn it one quarter-turn clockwise. Which way does it point?
questions.explanation: Down. Clockwise means the same turning direction as clock hands.

questions.question: You take 4 shells from a pile of 9 and put them in your pocket. How many shells are in your pocket?
questions.explanation: 4. Count the shells taken, not those remaining.

questions.question: A bag holds only red, blue and yellow counters, at least 4 of each. How many must you take without looking to be certain of two of the same colour?
questions.explanation: 4. Three could all be different; a fourth must repeat a colour.

questions.question: Five children each get 2 stickers. There are 13 stickers at the start. How many remain?
A frog jumps 4 stones forward, then 1 stone back, each round. It starts at stone 0. What stone is it on after 3 complete rounds?
questions.explanation: 9. Each complete round gains 3 stones; 3 x 3 = 9.
